frequency_question: How often does the federal government successfully revoke an institutional or programmatic accreditor's status rather than renewing, probation, or voluntary withdrawal?
membership_rule: Includes formal administrative proceedings by the U.S. Department of Education targeting a recognized accreditor's agency status; excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor compliance warnings without revocation attempts.

cases.name: ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) Termination
ABA (American Bar Association) Initial De-recognition Threat and Review

coverage_note: 2 named; believed roughly 3 to 4 major high-stakes federal challenges to national/programmatic accreditors in total over this era.
known_gaps: Lower-profile programmatic accreditor disputes that did not reach the secretary level or public administrative record.
skeleton: Total formal de-recognition proceedings initiated against major national/programmatic accreditors over three decades, scaled by the rarity of final executed terminations versus settlements or restorations.
multiplier: 2 attempted major revocation processes, resulting in 1 complete termination (ACICS) and 1 survival/retained recognition (ABA prior review).
validity_reason: Relies on statutory standards under the Higher Education Act which remain stable across administrations, though political appointment priorities shift every 4 to 8 years.
